messages:
Marta G.: Heads up — customer AcmePay (private deployment) started seeing KMS decrypt failures right after their scheduled key rotation. Error in logs: InvalidCiphertextException + "EncryptionContext mismatch". Tokens failing to decrypt, services degraded.
Jordan Chen: Ugh. Do we have the key ARN + account id? Also any rotation event from kms-bot?
kms-bot: Key rotation completed for arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 at 2025-11-05T14:02:03Z
Jordan Chen: Thanks. Two quick suspects: 1) the caller lost the EncryptionContext (must match exactly), or 2) key policy / IAM missing kms:Decrypt for our role. Marta — can you ask customer to run a quick local decrypt to confirm?
Marta G.: They gave ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01, acct 123456789012. They said they encrypted with encryption_context {"env":"prod","tenant":"acmepay"}. Their ops says our private node might be invoking Decrypt without the same context.
Rajesh Patel: If the encryption context doesn’t match, KMS returns InvalidCiphertextException — expected. Repro steps for the customer (privately):
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://token.bin \
  --encryption-context '{"env":"prod","tenant":"acmepay"}' \
  --output text --query Plaintext | base64 --decode
```
Then try the same *without* --encryption-context — should fail. Also check CloudTrail for eventName="Decrypt" and inspect requestParameters.encryptionContext.
Jordan Chen: On our side, ensure the private proxy forwards the encryption context. Our code path uses: 
```
KMSClient.decrypt(CiphertextBlob=ciphertext, EncryptionContext={'env':'prod','tenant':'acmepay'})
```
But I know there are some older proxies that dropped the header.
Anya Li: Note — key rotation that simply re-keys material under the same CMK keeps the same key ARN; but if customer created a new CMK and rewrapped data manually without updating consumers, you'll see this. Also confirm key policy allows arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-kms to call Decrypt/GenerateDataKey as appropriate.
Rajesh Patel: Can you share a small sample ciphertext (safe subset) and I’ll try to reproduce?
Marta G.: Sent sample blob to ticket (not pasted here).
Rajesh Patel: Reproduced locally — our private proxy call was missing EncryptionContext for that codepath. Created a temporary grant and patched the proxy to forward context. Commands used for debug: 
```
aws kms create-grant \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-kms \
  --operations Decrypt \
  --name temp-redwood-debug
```
Patch rolled to us-east-1 private nodes (canary -> 3 nodes).
Jordan Chen: Can customer retest?
Marta G.: Customer retried and reports success — tokens decrypted, services back online. :white_check_mark:
Anya Li: Good. Next steps: capture CloudTrail Decrypt entries (for audit), update CMK key policy to permanently allow our principal (instead of relying on temporary grants), and add e2e test that verifies EncryptionContext is forwarded. Also recommend customers enable automatic key rotation on the same CMK (enableKeyRotation) rather than creating separate CMKs that change ARNs.
Jordan Chen: I’ll file a short postmortem / change request: add unit + e2e tests, ensure proxy code paths all forward EncryptionContext, and update runbook for oncall. Assign to Rajesh for the policy change.
Marta G.: I’ll update the support ticket with root-cause and steps we took. Thanks all.
Anya Li: Marking follow-ups: capture CloudTrail, update key policy, add test. Will loop in legal/compliance if audit retention needs to be extended.
Jordan Chen: Great. Closing the incident once the policy change is in prod.
Marta G.: Customer has been informed. Closing for now, will reopen if anything else pops up.
